Nucleome Browser" ], "Omics": [ "Epigenomics", "Genomics" ], "Data Entities": [ "Region" ], "Foundational Knowledge": "The 4D Nucleome (4DN) project generates and provides information on the spatial organization of chromatin and the genome within the nucleus of human and model organism cells at multiple scales (entire chromosomes, specific genomic loci, individual genes and elements), time points (single time, time course) and perturbations (genetic, environmental). Together this information represents a public resource for studying interactions between genomic regions and the nuclear environment as well as how these interactions impact gene expression, function, development, and disease.", "Primary Knowledge": "The 4DN project has provided seminal advances in our understanding of genome organization at multiple scales in human and model organism cells and key features such as chromatin looping, key proteins and factors and the underlying principles involved in genome organization, the relationship between genome organization and gene regulation and expression, and changes in genome organization and interactions across time, development, and disease.", "Secondary Knowledge": "Contact matrices derived from a sequencing-based experiment can be used to identify features of genome organization including (i) chromatin loops, describing a physical interaction between a pair of distant genomic regions such as enhancers-promoters and insulators; (ii) topologically-associating domains (TADs), describing broader stretches of the genome containing many interactions and that may help restrict the potential target genes of enhancers; and (iii) A/B compartments, describing active and inactive regions across entire chromosomes.", "Tertiary Knowledge": "Chromatin loops and other features such as TADs and A/B compartments represent an annotation of genes and the genome, and because genes and the genome have many other measurements and annotations in external datasets, there are numerous links that can be computed between 4DN data and other biological quantities.", "Foundational Knowledge detail": "Experimental design: The 4DN project consists of two main classes of experiments.
Sequence-based assays
Sequencing-based assays measure physical interactions between genomic regions in 3-dimensional space using high-throughput sequencing. There are multiple different iterations of sequencing-based assays, the most common of which is in situ Hi-C, which identifies interactions genome-wide in their natural context. Hi-C and Hi-C-based assays are part of a broader class of chromatin conformation capture (3C) techniques which use proximity ligation to link together fragments of DNA in close physical proximity.
  • Generation of 557 in situ Hi-C and other Hi-C-based assays from human and other organism cell lines, stem cell-derived cells, and primary cells
  • Generation of 56 single cell Hi-C-based assays from human and mouse cell lines, stem cell-derived cells, and primary cells
  • Generation of 296 other proximity- and non-proximity-based assays from human and other organism cell lines, stem cell-derived cells, and primary cells
  • Matrix of Interaction counts (contact matrix) between all pairs of genomic regions on a chromosome from sequence data of each assay
Microscopy-based assays
Microscopy-based assays measure physical interactions between genomic regions and the nuclear environment in 3-dimensional space using imaging. There are many different types of microscopy-based assays. The most common include multiplexed fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), where fluorophore-labeled oligonucleotides hybridized to specific genomic regions or RNA transcripts are imaged, or immunofluorescence where conjugated antibodies bound to proteins are imaged. Multiplexed FISH assays that measure genomic interactions at a locus are also known as ‘chromatin tracing’ assays. A further class of assays called single particle tracking (SPT) can measure the location and trajectory of a specific molecule in live cells over time.
  • Generation of 466 FISH assays including multiplexed FISH, DNA FISH and RNA FISH from human and other organism cell lines, stem cell-derived cells, and primary cells/tissues.
  • Generation of 138 immunofluorescence assays in human cell lines
  • Generation of 101 single particle tracking assays in human cell lines
  • Genomic regions at specific loci in spatial proximity from chromatin tracing data
  • Chromatin- and nuclear-based proteins in spatial proximity from imaging data
  • Spatial dynamics of chromatin from live cells, single particle tracking imaging data
In addition to these assays, the 4DN consortium has also generated additional 2-dimensional genomic sequence data such as RNA-seq to measure gene expression levels, ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN to measure transcription factor binding and histone modifications, and ATAC-seq to measure chromatin accessibility. These data can be used in the context of other 4DN data to understand the effects of genome organization on other aspects of gene regulation.", "Primary Knowledge detail": "Selected from 94 total publications, key findings from the 4DN project include:
Chromatin structure and looping in human cells:
Rao SS et al. A 3D map of the human genome at kilobase resolution reveals principles of chromatin looping. Cell 2014
  • Performed in situ Hi-C to reveal chromatin interactions in 9 nine cell types, including high-resolution (1kb) mapping of lymphoblastoid cells
  • Genome is organized in large contact domains which have distinct features such as histone mark patterns
  • Identified ~10k chromatin loops many of which describe enhancer-promoter interactions, and which correlate with gene activity and are conserved across species
  • The anchors of loops frequently occur near CTCF binding sites, and CTCF sites at each end of a loop are in convergent orientation
Jin F. A high-resolution map of the three-dimensional chromatin interactome in human cells. Nature 2013
  • Performed in situ Hi-C to reveal chromatin interactions in human fibroblast cells in baseline as well as after stimulation with TNF alpha
  • Identified millions of long-range chromatin interactions at a resolution of 5-10kb
  • Distal enhancers responsive to TNF alpha already interact with target gene promoters prior to signaling, and poised interactions are predictive of target genes of future signaling responses
  • Overall suggests that chromatin interactions once established are stable
Key factors and principles underlying chromatin structure:
Schwarzer W. Two independent modes of chromatin organization revealed by cohesin removal. Nature 2017
  • Performed Hi-C in liver of wild-type mice, mice with a tamoxifen-induced deletion of a Cohesin loading factor, and tamoxifen-treated control mice
  • Depletion of Cohesin loading in mouse liver resulted in widespread loss of TADs and chromatin loops
  • The broader A/B compartments, however, were unaffected by loss of Cohesin binding
  • Together the results demonstrate distinct mechanisms of genome organization whereby TADs and loops are Cohesin dependent whereas compartments are not
Rao SS. Cohesin Loss Eliminates All Loop Domains. Cell 2017.
  • Performed Hi-C in human colorectal carcinoma (HCT-116) cells with a deletion of the Cohesin component RAD21 and control
  • Depletion of Cohesin activity results in a total loss of chromatin looping but has no effect on A/B compartments or histone modifications
  • Loss of chromatin looping affects a specific set of active genes leading to effects on the regulation of other nearby genes
  • Restoring Cohesin activity results in chromatin loops reforming often within an hour
Nore EP. Targeted Degradation of CTCF Decouples Local Insulation of Chromosome Domains from Genomic Compartmentalization. Cell 2017.
  • Performed Hi-C and other 3C-based assays in mouse embryonic stem cells with depletion of CTCF activity and control cells
  • Depletion of CTCF results in loss of chromatin looping and insulation of enhancer activity through TADs, and restoring CTCF activity leads to re-forming of loops and insulation
  • By comparison, A/B compartments are unaffected by loss of CTCF
  • CTCF mediates insulator function by blocking enhancer activity and not by preventing heterochromatin formation
Chromatin structure and nuclear organization in single cells
Takei Y. Integrated spatial genomics reveals global architecture of single nuclei. Nature 2021.
  • Performed imaging of 3,660 genomic loci in single mouse embryonic stem cells using DNA FISH along with 17 histone marks, 70 transcripts, and subnuclear structures
  • Identified a large number of genomic loci with consistent activity and stable nuclear organization across individual cells, which represent ‘fixed’ points that anchor the nuclear organization of cells
  • Highly-expressed genes were pre-positioned at active nuclear zones and poised for rapid transcriptional activity (i.e. ‘bursting’)
  • Several histone marks such as H3K27me3 had broadly stable activity across generations, whereas other histone marks were less stable over shorter time periods.
Bintu B. Super-resolution chromatin tracing reveals domains and cooperative interactions in single cells. Science 2018.
  • Performed imaging of specific regions of chromosome 21 in thousands of human cells using multiplexed ultra-resolution FISH assays
  • Identified TAD structures in individual cells which had clear domain boundaries centered on CTCF and Cohesin binding sites and had globular structures
  • Depletion of Cohesin did not lead to loss of domain structures in individual cells but rather eliminated preferential boundaries at specific locations, and did not affect chromatin interactions.

These values are computed by the KC based on contact matrices generated by the 4DN consortium.

  • On the disease page: The probability that a gene is linked to a genetic variant causal for disease risk in a human cell line or cell type is computed by summing up the fine-mapping posterior probabilities of variants in chromatin loops to the promoter of expressed genes.

It also can be used as a global signature of genes or tissues within numerous downstream methods.", "Tertiary Knowledge": "Because gene expression values represent a signature of a tissue, and because genes have many other measurements in external datasets, GTEx values allow computation of numerous links between tissues and other biological quantities.", "Foundational Knowledge detail": "Experimental design: The GTEx project consists of three experiments
Adult GTEx (2010-2019)
  • Collection of tissue samples from up to 54 non-diseased sites in nearly 1,000 individuals
  • Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of donors
  • Determination of gene expression levels in each tissue by bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq)
  • Determination of gene expression levels in single cells for a subset of tissues from 16 donors, using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq)
  • Identification of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and splicing quantitative trait loci (sQTLs): genetic variants that are significantly associated with expression of specific genes or splicing of their transcripts
Developmental GTEx (2021-) (data not yet available)
  • Collection of tissue samples from up to 74 non-diseased sites in 120 donors, 30 each from 4 developmental windows (postnatal, early childhood, pre-pubertal, and post-pubertal)
  • Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of donors
  • Determination of gene expression levels in each tissue by bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq)
  • Investigation of a subset of tissues by single-cell RNA sequencing, chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomic assays
Non-human primate developmental GTEx (2022-) (data not yet available)
  • Collection of tissues from 24 organs from 12 rhesus macaque and 12 common marmoset individuals at each of 6-8 developmental stages, including prenatal developmental stages
  • Full-transcript genome sequencing of donors
  • Determination of gene expression levels in multiple tissues each from 12 individuals, sampled at 6 timepoints, by bulk RNA-sequencing
  • Generation of a first generation single-cell atlas covering 20 tissues for each species using single cell 10X multiome snRNA+ATAC sequencing
  • Annotation of functional elements by strategic epigenetic profiling using CHIP-seq and Hi-C
  • Investigation of a subset of tissues by spatial transcriptomic assays
", "Primary Knowledge detail": "Landmark findings from the GTEx project include:
GTEx Consortium. Human genomics. The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) pilot analysis: multitissue gene regulation in humans. Science. 2015.
  • First major publication of results from the GTEx (pilot) project
  • Analyzed RNA expression data from 1,641 samples across 43 tissues from 175 donors
  • Identified 6,486 unique eGenes (genes with significant cis-eQTLs) across 9 tissues
  • Quantified regulatory diversity by allele-specific gene expression
  • One of the first systematic surveys of gene expression across tissues and how eQTLs impact these via tissue-specific and shared effects, with implications for our understanding of gene regulatory networks and complex trait associations.
GTEx Consortium. Genetic effects on gene expression across human tissues. Nature. 2017.
  • Results from the GTEx v6 release
  • RNA expression data from 7,051 samples across 44 tissues from 449 donors
  • Higher resolution maps of eQTLs relative to the pilot project: 152,869 cis-eQTLs for 19,725 genes, and trans-eQTLs for 93 genes and 112 loci
  • Showed substantial tissue specificity of eQTLs: most are either shared across most tissues or specific to a small subset of tissues
  • Demonstrated that multi-tissue, multi-individual data can localize genetic associations to genes and pathways
GTEx Consortium. The GTEx Consortium atlas of genetic regulatory effects across human tissues. Science. 2020.
  • Results for the GTEx v8 release
  • RNA expression levels in 15,201 samples across 49 tissues from 838 donors
  • Showed, with sufficient data, that regulatory associations are found for almost all genes: cis-eQTLs for 18,262 protein-coding genes and 5,006 lincRNA genes
  • Investigated splicing QTLs and showed that these exist for most genes: cis-sQTLs for 12,828 protein-coding genes and 1,600 lincRNA genes
  • Defined a consensus set of 24,740 cis-eQTLs across all tissues by fine-mapping
  • Showed cell type composition is critical to gene regulatory mechanisms in humans
Kim-Hellmuth* S, Aguet* F, et al. Cell type specific genetic regulation of gene expression across human tissues. Science. 2020.
  • Mapped interactions between estimates of cell type abundance and genotype to study cell type-interaction eQTLs and sQTLs
  • Identified cell type-interaction eQTLs for 3,347 protein coding and lincRNA genes in 43 cell type-tissue pairs
  • Identified cell type-interaction sQTLs for 987 protein coding and lincRNA genes in 43 cell type-tissue pairs
  • Showed that cell type-interaction eQTLs provide finer resolution to tissue-specificity than conventional bulk tissue cis-eQTLs
  • Showed contribution of cell type-interaction eQTLs to numerous complex traits and demonstrated their ability to identify novel links between genetic variants and gene expression
Eraslan G, et al. Single-nucleus cross-tissue molecular reference maps toward understanding disease gene function. Science. 2022.
  • Applied four snRNA-seq methods to 8 tissue types across 16 donors to understand the cellular and tissue contexts in which genes are expressed
  • Integrated 209,126 snRNA-seq profiles across tissues, donors, and methods
  • Identified shared and tissue-specific features of cell populations
  • Hypothesized cell types and modules that might contribute to monogenic disease and complex traits
", "Secondary Knowledge detail": "In the KC we currently represent two types of secondary knowledge extracted from GTEx.
  • On the Gene page: The absolute expression levels of a gene across all tissues indicates the degree to which it is observed in each tissue. These values are directly extracted from the GTEx project.
  • On the Gene page: The tissue-specific expression values (t-stat) of a gene indicate the degree to which it is specific to each tissue, which is often a better indicator of whether the gene is relevant to a disease characterized by dysfunction of the tissue. These values are computed by applying a method (see Documentation) that measures the degree to which the tissue predicts high expression values of the gene.
", "Tertiary Knowledge detail": "In the KC we currently represent one type of tertiary knowledge that results from integrating GTEx data with genetic association statistics.
On the disease page: The degree to which genetic associations for the disease act through each tissue is shown by calculating the enrichment of associations within regions nearby genes with the most tissue-specific expression. These values are computed by applying Stratified LD-score regression (see Documentation) to the GTEx t-stat values and genetic associations from the Association to Function Knowledge Portal.",
